facts.text: Hysham was founded around a Northern Pacific Railroad siding built to unload supplies for the Flying E ranch.
The town was named after Charlie Hysham, a rancher who had moved away but was honored by the new settlement.
The historic Yucca Theatre, built in 1931 by Dave and Jim Manning, stands as a mission‑style landmark on Hysham’s main street.
The Treasure County 89ers Museum on main street showcases fossils, Crow history, and homesteader artifacts, telling Hysham’s story.
Lockard’s first building and the general store, which also served as the first post office, marked the town’s early commercial hub north of the tracks.
Howrey Island, Myers Bridge, and the Isaac Homestead Wilderness Management Area offer outdoor recreation just outside Hysham, linking the town to regional natural sites.
